questions.question: How do you return JSON from a Rails controller?
questions.title: Returning JSON in Rails
questions.direct_answer: render json: renders JSON: render json: Post.all (serializes with to_json), render json: post, status: :created (with a status), render json: { error: 'invalid' }, status: :unprocessable_entity (a manual error shape). For a model, to_json includes its attributes; you can pass only: [:id, :title] to limit fields, include: [:comments] for associations, methods: [:url] for computed fields. For complex shapes, use a serializer (ActiveModel::Serializers or jsonapi-serializer) that defines the JSON shape in a class, so the view of the model is separate from the model. head :no_content returns a status with no body (204).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know render json: (with status/only/include), head :no_content, and that serializers separate the JSON shape for complex models.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Returning the whole model with all attributes (over-exposure), or building JSON with string concatenation (use render json: / serializers).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: render json: obj, status: :created; only:/include: to limit fields; head :no_content for no body. Serializers separate the JSON shape for complex models.

sections.title: render json and Serializers
sections.content: render json renders JSON: render json Post dot all serializes with to_json; render json post, status created with a status; render json error invalid, status unprocessable_entity for a manual error shape. For a model, to_json includes its attributes; you can pass only: id title to limit fields, include: comments for associations, and methods: url for computed fields. For complex shapes, use a serializer — ActiveModel::Serializers or jsonapi-serializer — that defines the JSON shape in a class, so the view of the model is separate from the model itself. head no_content returns a status with no body, 204. Pick render json for simple cases and a serializer once the shape grows.

sections.title: Model -> JSON
sections.content:
render json serializes; only/include limit fields; a serializer class for complex shapes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[model] --> R[render json: -> to_json]
  R --> O[only:/include: limit fields]
  R --> S[serializer class -> controlled JSON shape]
```

sections.title: JSON responses
sections.content:
```ruby
# Basic render json (uses to_json)
render json: Post.all

# With a status code
render json: post, status: :created       # 201

# Limit fields and include associations
render json: Post.all, only: [:id, :title],
              include: { comments: { only: [:id, :body] } }

# Add a computed method
render json: post, methods: [:url]
# (define `def url; "/posts/#{id}"; end` on the model)

# A manual error shape
render json: { error: 'invalid', details: post.errors.full_messages },
       status: :unprocessable_entity   # 422

# No body, just a status (e.g. 204 after destroy)
head :no_content

# Complex shape -> a serializer class (ActiveModel::Serializers)
class PostSerializer < ActiveModel::Serializer
  attributes :id, :title, :author_name
  def author_name; object.user.name; end
end
render json: post, serializer: PostSerializer
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Returning the whole model with all attributes — over-exposure; use only: to limit.
Building JSON with string concatenation — use render json: or a serializer.
Not using a serializer once the JSON shape is complex (it separates the shape).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: render json: obj serializes with to_json; add status: :created for a code.
Limit fields with only: [:id, :title]; include associations with include:.
Add computed fields with methods: [:url] (define the method on the model).
head :no_content returns a status with no body (204, after destroy).
For complex shapes, use a serializer class (ActiveModel::Serializers) to separate the JSON view.
